title: Mutton Soup (Paya Style Light)
intro: A warming, aromatic mutton bone soup with ginger, pepper and whole spices. Slow-cooked bones give collagen-rich broth. Skim the fat for a light version. Ideal on cold evenings.
ingredients: 300 g mutton bones with some meat
steps: Pressure cook all ingredients for 8-10 whistles.
Cool and skim off fat from the top.
Strain the broth and shred the meat.
Reheat with salt and extra pepper.
Garnish with coriander.

title: Egg-Free Chicken Seekh Kebab
intro: Spiced chicken mince pressed around skewers and grilled until smoky and juicy. Unlike restaurant versions, these need no egg, breadcrumbs or butter, so they stay lean. Grated onion and fresh herbs keep them moist. Serve with onion salad, lemon and mint chutney.
ingredients: 1 tsp garam masala and 1/2 tsp cumin powder
steps: Mix mince with onion, ginger-garlic, chillies, spices, herbs and salt.
Knead well and chill for 20 minutes so it firms up.
Wet your hands and press the mixture around skewers into long kebabs.
Brush lightly with oil.
Grill or air-fry at 200 C for 12-15 minutes, turning once.

title: Chicken Lettuce Wraps
intro: Spicy, dry-cooked chicken mince spooned into crisp lettuce cups instead of rotis. They are fresh, crunchy and very low in carbohydrates. Top with chopped onion, coriander and a squeeze of lemon. A fun, light dinner the whole family enjoys.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp each cumin, coriander and chilli powder
steps: Saute onion and ginger-garlic in oil until soft.
Add mince and spices and cook on high heat, breaking up lumps.
Add capsicum and salt and cook until dry, about 8 minutes.
Wash and pat dry the lettuce leaves.
Spoon mince into each leaf, squeeze lemon and garnish.

title: Methi Chicken
intro: Chicken simmered in a light onion-tomato gravy with plenty of fresh fenugreek leaves. Methi gives a gently bitter, aromatic flavour that pairs beautifully with chicken. It adds fibre and helps control cravings. Serve with phulka for a satisfying dinner.
ingredients: 1 tsp coriander powder and 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Saute onions in oil until golden, then add ginger-garlic.
Add tomatoes and spices and cook till soft.
Add chicken and cook on high for 8-10 minutes.
Add methi and 1/2 cup water and cook covered 10 minutes.
Simmer until chicken is tender and serve.

title: Chicken Kathi Roll (Whole Wheat)
intro: Smoky chicken tikka wrapped in a whole wheat roti with crunchy onions, mint chutney and lemon. It is the healthy version of the famous Kolkata street food. Hung curd replaces mayonnaise, keeping it light. Perfect for lunch on the go.
steps: Warm rotis on a tawa without oil.
Mix chutney and hung curd and spread on each roti.
Lay lettuce, chicken tikka and onion along the centre.
Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice.
Roll tightly, wrap in foil and serve.

title: Chicken Saag
intro: Tender chicken cooked in a smooth, spiced spinach gravy, a lighter non-veg cousin of palak paneer. It packs protein and iron into one bowl. The spinach gives a creamy texture without cream. Serve with roti or millet.
steps: Blend blanched spinach to a smooth puree.
Saute onion and ginger-garlic in oil, add tomatoes and cook soft.
Add chicken and garam masala and cook 10 minutes.
Pour in the spinach puree and salt.
Simmer covered 10 minutes till chicken is tender.

title: Grilled Fish with Herbs
intro: Fish fillets rubbed with garlic, lemon zest, mixed herbs and black pepper, then grilled until just flaky. It is simple, elegant and ready in 25 minutes. Fish provides lean protein and heart-healthy omega-3 fats. Serve with sauteed or steamed vegetables.
steps: Pat fillets dry.
Rub with garlic, lemon zest, herbs, pepper, salt and oil.
Rest for 10 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear 3-4 minutes per side.
Squeeze lemon juice and serve with vegetables.

title: Chicken Biryani (Brown Rice)
intro: A fragrant dum biryani made with brown rice, generous chicken and just a teaspoon of ghee. We use more chicken and less rice than usual, so every plate is protein-heavy. Mint, saffron and whole spices give the classic aroma. Serve with cucumber raita.
ingredients: 1 cup brown basmati rice, soaked 1 hour
Bay leaf, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon
Handful mint and few saffron strands
steps: Marinate chicken with curd, biryani masala and salt for 30 minutes.
Boil rice with whole spices and salt until 70% cooked, drain.
Brown onions in ghee, add chicken and cook till almost done.
Layer rice over chicken with mint and saffron milk.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat 20 minutes.

title: Chilli Chicken (Healthy)
intro: The Indo-Chinese favourite made without deep frying or a thick cornflour batter. Chicken is pan-seared and tossed with onion, capsicum, garlic and green chillies in a light sauce. It is spicy, glossy and satisfying. Serve with cauliflower rice.
steps: Season chicken with salt and pepper and sear in oil till golden, remove.
Stir-fry garlic and chillies, then onion and capsicum on high heat.
Add soy, vinegar and chilli sauce.
Add cornflour slurry and stir till glossy.
Toss in the chicken and serve hot.

title: Mutton Keema with Lauki
intro: Lean mutton mince cooked with diced bottle gourd in a spicy masala. The lauki soaks up flavour and adds volume, so you eat a satisfying portion with fewer calories. Mutton provides iron and vitamin B12. Serve with phulka.
ingredients: 1 tsp coriander powder and 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Saute onion and ginger-garlic in oil till golden.
Add tomato and spices and cook soft.
Add keema and cook on high 10 minutes, breaking lumps.
Add lauki and 1/2 cup water and cook covered 10 minutes.
Dry off any moisture and garnish.
benefits: Lauki adds volume with few calories.

title: Chicken Malai Tikka (Light)
intro: Creamy, mild white tikka where cream is replaced by hung curd and a spoon of cheese spread. Cardamom and white pepper give it a delicate flavour. It is juicy, tender and loved by kids. Grill or air-fry and serve with mint chutney.
steps: Rub chicken with ginger-garlic, salt and lemon for 15 minutes.
Whisk curd, cheese spread, cardamom, pepper, chilli and oil.
Coat chicken and marinate 1 hour.
Thread on skewers.
Grill or air-fry at 200 C for 15 minutes.

title: Fish Moilee (Light)
intro: A gentle Kerala fish stew in a fragrant turmeric and light coconut milk broth with ginger, green chillies and curry leaves. It is mild, soothing and full of lean protein. in check. Serve with a small portion of red rice.
steps: Rub fish with turmeric and salt.
Heat oil and saute onion, ginger, chillies and curry leaves till soft.
Add turmeric and 1 cup water and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the fish and cook 6 minutes.
Add coconut milk and simmer 2 minutes without boiling.

title: Pepper Chicken Dry
intro: A Chettinad-style dry chicken roast with freshly crushed black pepper, curry leaves and onions. It is bold, fiery and very low in carbs. Pepper's piperine supports digestion and metabolism. Serve with salad or a millet roti.
steps: Heat oil, add fennel and curry leaves, then onion.
Add ginger-garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add chicken, turmeric and salt and cook covered 10 minutes.
Add crushed pepper and roast on high until dry.
Garnish with more curry leaves.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala (Light)
intro: Grilled chicken tikka simmered in a smoky, spiced onion-tomato masala finished with curd and kasuri methi. You get restaurant flavour at home-cooked calories. No butter, no cream. Serve with phulka and salad.
ingredients: 1 tsp kashmiri chilli and 1 tsp garam masala
steps: Saute onions in oil until golden, add ginger-garlic.
Add tomato puree and spices and cook till oil separates.
Lower heat and stir in whisked curd.
Add tikka and 1/2 cup water and simmer 5 minutes.
Crush kasuri methi over the top and serve.

title: Prawn Stir Fry
intro: Juicy prawns tossed with garlic, chilli flakes, onion and capsicum on high heat. Prawns cook in just 3-4 minutes, so dinner is ready in 15. They are very lean and rich in minerals like selenium and iodine. Serve with salad or cauliflower rice.
steps: Season prawns with salt and chilli flakes.
Heat oil on high and saute garlic for 30 seconds.
Add prawns and cook 2 minutes until pink.
Add onion and capsicum and toss 2 minutes.
Add soy sauce, toss and garnish with spring onion.

title: Chicken Ghee Roast (Light)
intro: A fiery Mangalorean roast where chicken is coated in a paste of roasted byadgi chillies, spices, tamarind and garlic. We use only one spoon of ghee instead of the usual several. It is tangy, spicy and deeply flavourful. Serve with salad or neer dosa.
ingredients: 1 tsp coriander seeds and 1/2 tsp cumin seeds
steps: Dry-roast chillies, coriander and cumin, grind with tamarind and garlic.
Marinate chicken with curd, salt and half the paste for 30 minutes.
Heat ghee, fry remaining paste for 2 minutes.
Add chicken and cook covered 10 minutes.
Uncover and roast until dry, adding curry leaves.

title: High Protein Paneer Omelette
intro: A fluffy masala omelette stuffed with crumbled paneer, onion, tomato and green chillies. Combining eggs and paneer creates a breakfast with over 25 hours and reduces mid-morning snacking. Cook it in a non-stick pan with just a few drops of oil.
steps: Whisk eggs and egg white with turmeric, pepper and salt until frothy.
Stir in onion, tomato, chilli and coriander.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan and pour in the mixture.
Sprinkle paneer over one half while the top is still soft.
Fold, cook 1 minute on each side and serve.
benefits: Over 25 g protein in one meal.
Eggs provide choline and vitamin B12.

title: Egg Bhurji
intro: Spicy Indian scrambled eggs cooked with onions, tomatoes and green chillies. It is a quick, satisfying breakfast or dinner. Add extra egg whites to boost protein without adding fat. Wrap in lettuce or eat with a single multigrain toast.
steps: Heat oil and saute onion till soft.
Add chilli, tomato, turmeric and masala, cook 2 minutes.
Pour in beaten eggs and salt.
Stir gently on low heat till softly set.
Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Egg Curry (Light)
intro: Boiled eggs simmered in a homestyle onion-tomato gravy made with just a teaspoon of oil. It is comforting, protein-rich and budget-friendly. Use 1 whole egg and extra whites to manage calories. Serve with phulka or cauliflower rice.
ingredients: 1 tsp coriander powder and 1/2 tsp garam masala
steps: Lightly prick the boiled eggs and toss in a pinch of turmeric and chilli.
Saute onions and ginger-garlic in oil until golden.
Add tomato puree and spices, cook till oil separates.
Add 1 cup water and simmer 5 minutes.
Add eggs, simmer 3 minutes and garnish.
benefits: Rich in vitamins D and B12.

title: Egg White Veggie Omelette
intro: A light, fluffy omelette made from spinach, capsicum and onion. It is almost pure protein with very few calories. A great choice for dinner or a pre-workout meal. Season with pepper and herbs.
steps: Whisk egg whites with salt and pepper till frothy.
Saute vegetables in a few drops of oil for 2 minutes.
Pour egg whites over the vegetables.
Cover and cook on low heat until set.
Fold, sprinkle oregano and serve.
benefits: Lean protein with almost no fat.

title: Masala Boiled Egg Salad
intro: Boiled eggs tossed with cucumber, onion, tomato and a chaat masala-lemon dressing. It is a crunchy, tangy salad that works as a meal or snack. Takes 15 minutes and travels well. Add sprouts for more fibre.
steps: Boil eggs for 10 minutes, cool and quarter.
Chop all vegetables.
Combine vegetables with salt, pepper, chaat masala and lemon.
Gently fold in eggs.
Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Egg Muffins with Vegetables
intro: Mini egg muffins baked with spinach, tomato, onion and a little cheese. Make a batch on Sunday and reheat for quick breakfasts all week. They are portion-controlled and kid-friendly. No flour needed.
steps: Preheat oven to 180 C and grease a muffin tray.
Whisk eggs with salt, pepper and chilli flakes.
Divide vegetables into the muffin cups.
Pour egg mixture over and top with cheese.
Bake 18-20 minutes until puffed and set.

title: Egg Dosa
intro: A crisp dosa topped with a beaten egg, onions and chillies. It adds protein to a regular dosa and keeps you full for longer. Use ragi or oats dosa batter for extra fibre. Serve with chutney.
steps: Spread batter thinly on a hot tawa.
Break the egg on top and spread it evenly.
Sprinkle onion, chilli, pepper, salt and coriander.
Drizzle few drops of oil and cook till crisp.
Fold and serve.
benefits: Adds protein to a carb meal.

title: Egg Bhurji Wrap
intro: Spicy egg bhurji rolled in a whole wheat roti with onions and mint chutney. Perfect for lunch boxes and busy mornings. It is balanced with protein, carbs and fibre. Add lettuce for crunch.
steps: Make egg bhurji with onion, tomato and spices.
Warm the roti on a tawa.
Spread chutney and lay lettuce.
Add bhurji and roll tightly.
Cut in half and serve.

title: Egg Drop Soup (Indian Style)
intro: A light ginger-garlic broth with ribbons of beaten egg and vegetables. It is very low in calories yet warm and filling. Great for dinner on light days. Ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Boil stock with ginger, garlic and vegetables for 5 minutes.
Season with soy, salt and pepper.
Stir the soup in a circle and slowly pour in beaten eggs.
Let ribbons form for 30 seconds.
Garnish with spring onion.

title: Palak Egg Curry
intro: Halved boiled eggs nestled in a smooth, spiced spinach gravy. This dish combines the complete protein of eggs with the iron and fibre of spinach. It is creamy without any cream and ready in 30 minutes. Serve with phulka or millet roti.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp garam masala and cumin powder
steps: Blend the blanched spinach into a smooth puree.
Saute onion and ginger-garlic in oil, add tomato and cook soft.
Add spices and spinach puree and simmer 5 minutes.
Gently place the halved eggs in the gravy.
Simmer 2 minutes and serve.

title: Green Weight Loss Smoothie
intro: A refreshing blend of spinach, cucumber, green apple, mint and lemon with a spoon of chia seeds. It is light, hydrating and full of fibre. Drink it in the morning or as a mid-meal snack to curb cravings. No sugar added.
steps: Wash and chop spinach, cucumber and apple.
Add everything to a blender with water.
Blend until smooth.
Stir in soaked chia seeds.
Serve chilled.

title: Jeera Water
intro: An age-old Indian remedy made by boiling cumin seeds in water. Drink it warm on an empty stomach to kick-start digestion. It reduces bloating and supports metabolism. Add lemon for flavour.
steps: Soak cumin seeds in water overnight.
Boil the water with seeds for 5 minutes.
Strain into a cup.
Add lemon and black salt if desired.
Sip warm on an empty stomach.

title: Cinnamon Ajwain Tea
intro: A warming, caffeine-free herbal tea brewed from cinnamon bark and ajwain seeds. Sip it after meals to soothe digestion and reduce bloating. Cinnamon is known to help steady blood sugar, which can curb sugar cravings. A comforting evening ritual that replaces milky sweet tea.
steps: Bring water to a boil with the cinnamon stick and ajwain.
Simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes until golden.
Strain into cups.
Let it cool slightly before adding honey and lemon.
Sip warm after meals.

title: Masala Chaas (Buttermilk)
intro: A chilled, spiced buttermilk blended with roasted cumin, ginger, mint and coriander. It is India's original digestive drink and a perfect replacement for sugary soft drinks. With only about 50 calories per glass, it cools the body and supports gut health. Drink it with or after lunch.
steps: Add curd, water, ginger and chilli to a blender.
Blend until frothy and smooth.
Stir in cumin, black salt and salt.
Add finely chopped mint and coriander.
Serve chilled with a pinch of cumin on top.

title: Lemon Ginger Detox Water
intro: A refreshing infused water with lemon slices, fresh ginger and mint. Keeping a bottle nearby makes it easy to drink more water through the day, which helps control hunger. It has no sugar and almost no calories. Refill the jug two or three times with the same ingredients.
steps: Add lemon, ginger, mint and cucumber to a large jug.
Lightly crush the mint with a spoon.
Pour water over and stir.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to infuse.
Sip through the day and refill with fresh water.

title: Banana Oats Protein Smoothie
intro: A thick, creamy breakfast smoothie made with banana, oats, curd, milk and a spoon of peanut butter. It gives a balance of protein, fibre and healthy fats that keeps you full for hours. The banana sweetens it naturally, so no sugar is needed. Ideal before or after a workout.
steps: Add oats to the blender first and pulse to a powder.
Add banana, curd, milk, peanut butter and flaxseed.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Add ice and blend again, thin with water if needed.
Pour into a glass and dust with cinnamon.

title: Beetroot Carrot Juice
intro: A vibrant ruby juice of beetroot, carrot, amla and ginger. It is packed with antioxidants, iron and vitamin C. Blending without straining keeps the fibre, so it fills you up and does not spike blood sugar. Drink it fresh in the morning.
steps: Chop beetroot, carrots, amla and ginger.
Blend with water until completely smooth.
Do not strain, to keep all the fibre.
Stir in lemon juice and black salt.
Serve immediately over ice.

title: Methi Seed Water
intro: Fenugreek seeds soaked overnight make a simple, traditional morning drink. The soaked seeds release soluble fibre into the water, which helps you feel full and supports healthy blood sugar levels. It takes less than a minute to prepare. Chew the softened seeds for extra benefit.
steps: Rinse methi seeds and place them in a glass of water at night.
Leave to soak for 8 hours.
In the morning, warm the water slightly if you like.
Add lemon or cinnamon if desired and drink on an empty stomach.
Chew the soaked seeds and wait 30 minutes before breakfast.

title: Coconut Water Mint Cooler
intro: Fresh tender coconut water shaken with crushed mint, lemon and a pinch of black salt. It is naturally sweet and full of electrolytes like potassium. A perfect post-workout drink and far healthier than packaged sports drinks. Serve ice-cold on summer afternoons.
steps: Gently crush mint leaves in the bottom of a glass.
Add lemon juice and black salt.
Pour in chilled coconut water.
Add cucumber slices and ice.
Stir well and serve immediately.

title: Turmeric Golden Milk (Light)
intro: Warm low-fat milk simmered with turmeric, ginger, cinnamon and a pinch of black pepper, which helps the body absorb turmeric. It is a soothing bedtime drink that calms late-night cravings. It supplies protein and calcium. Sweeten with stevia if you need it.
steps: Pour milk into a small pan.
Add turmeric, pepper, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg.
Simmer on low for 5 minutes, stirring.
Strain into a cup.
Sweeten lightly if needed and sip warm before bed.

title: Lauki Ki Barfi
intro: A soft, fudge-like barfi made with grated bottle gourd, milk and a little khoya-free milk powder, sweetened with dates or stevia. It satisfies sweet cravings with far fewer calories than regular mithai. Cardamom and pistachios make it festive. Perfect for Diwali on a diet.
steps: Saute lauki in ghee for 5 minutes till the raw smell goes.
Add milk and cook stirring till it is absorbed.
Add dates and milk powder and cook till the mixture leaves the pan.
Stir in cardamom and spread on a greased plate.
Top with pistachios, cool and cut into squares.
benefits: About half the calories of regular

title: Date and Nut Ladoo
intro: Soft, chewy energy balls made with dates, almonds, walnuts and flaxseed, with no added sugar at all. Dates provide natural sweetness and fibre, while nuts add healthy fats that keep you satisfied. One or two ladoos are perfect before a workout or when a sweet craving hits. They keep for two weeks in an airtight jar.
steps: Dry-roast almonds, walnuts and flaxseeds for 3 minutes and chop coarsely.
Blend dates into a sticky paste.
Warm ghee in a pan, add the date paste and cook 2 minutes.
Mix in nuts, flaxseed and cardamom and turn off the heat.
Grease palms, shape small ladoos and roll in coconut.

title: Ragi Halwa
intro: A warm, glossy halwa made from roasted finger millet flour, jaggery and just a teaspoon of ghee. Ragi gives it a deep chocolatey colour and a nutty flavour. It is rich in calcium and fibre, so it satisfies without a sugar crash. Serve warm topped with sliced almonds.
steps: Roast ragi flour in ghee on low heat for 5 minutes until aromatic.
Warm water or milk and dissolve the jaggery in it.
Slowly pour the liquid into the ragi while stirring to avoid lumps.
Cook, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Add cardamom, garnish with almonds and serve warm.

title: Oats Kheer
intro: A creamy, comforting kheer made by simmering rolled oats in low-fat milk and sweetening with chopped dates. Saffron and cardamom give it the familiar festive aroma. Oats add fibre, making this dessert surprisingly filling. Enjoy warm or chilled.
steps: Lightly roast oats in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Bring milk to a boil and add the oats.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring often.
Add dates, cardamom and saffron and cook 2 minutes more.
Garnish with nuts and serve.

title: Shrikhand with Fruits
intro: A thick, velvety Maharashtrian dessert of hung curd flavoured with saffron and cardamom, lightly sweetened and topped with fresh fruit. It is high in protein and probiotics. Using honey or stevia keeps the sugar low. Cool, creamy and very easy to make.
ingredients: 1 tsp honey or stevia to taste
Few saffron strands soaked in 1 tbsp warm milk
steps: Whisk hung curd until completely smooth.
Add sweetener, saffron milk and cardamom and mix well.
Chill for 30 minutes.
Spoon into bowls and top with fresh fruits.
Garnish with pistachios and serve.

title: Apple Cinnamon Baked Dessert
intro: Apple slices tossed with cinnamon and a little honey, topped with an oat-and-nut crumble and baked until soft and bubbling. It tastes like apple pie without the buttery pastry. The apples are naturally sweet and full of fibre. Serve warm with a spoon of hung curd.
steps: Toss apple slices with cinnamon, honey and lemon.
Arrange in a small baking dish.
Mix oats, nuts and ghee and sprinkle over the apples.
Bake at 180 C for 20 minutes until golden.
Serve warm.

title: Besan Ladoo (Jaggery)
intro: The classic Diwali ladoo made lighter with less ghee and jaggery powder in place of sugar. Slow-roasting the besan brings out a deep, nutty aroma. Besan provides more protein than most sweets. One ladoo is enough to satisfy a craving.
steps: Heat ghee and add besan.
Roast on low heat, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Cool until warm but not hot.
Mix in jaggery, cardamom and nuts.
Shape into small ladoos.

title: Makhana Kheer
intro: Roasted fox nuts simmered in low-fat milk with dates, cardamom and saffron. Makhana is low in calories, high in protein and naturally gluten-free. Crushing half of it makes the kheer thick and creamy. A light dessert that is perfect during fasting days.
steps: Dry-roast makhana until crisp, then crush half of it coarsely.
Bring milk to a boil.
Add crushed and whole makhana and simmer 10 minutes.
Add dates, cardamom and saffron and cook 3 minutes more.
Garnish with almonds and serve warm or chilled.

title: Chia Mango Pudding
intro: Chia seeds soaked overnight in cardamom-scented milk and layered with fresh mango puree. The seeds swell into a creamy pudding that is rich in fibre and omega-3 fats. Ripe mango gives all the sweetness you need. Make it the night before for a ready dessert.
steps: Stir chia seeds into milk with cardamom and honey.
Rest 10 minutes, stir again to break lumps.
Refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
Blend half the mango into a puree and dice the rest.
Layer chia, mango puree and diced mango in a glass, top with pistachios.

title: Dates Coconut Rolls
intro: No-cook rolls of date paste studded with nuts and coated in desiccated coconut, then chilled and sliced into rounds. They look like festive mithai yet contain no added sugar. Each slice gives quick energy and fibre. Ideal for gifting during festivals.
steps: Blend dates into a smooth paste.
Cook the paste in ghee for 2-3 minutes until it comes together.
Mix in nuts and cardamom and let it cool slightly.
Shape into a log and roll in coconut and poppy seeds.
Chill 30 minutes and slice into rounds.

title: Green Chutney
intro: A bright, fresh chutney of coriander, mint, green chillies, ginger and lemon. It adds big flavour to chillas, tikkas and sandwiches with almost no calories. Add a spoon of roasted chana for body. Keeps a week in the fridge.
steps: Wash herbs well.
Blend with chillies, ginger, chana and lemon.
Add ice water to keep it green.
Season with salt and black salt.
Store in a jar.

title: Hung Curd Dip
intro: A thick, creamy dip of hung curd with grated garlic, fresh herbs, lemon and black pepper. It is a perfect substitute for mayonnaise in sandwiches, wraps and salads. Each spoon gives protein and probiotics with very few calories. Serve with carrot and cucumber sticks.
ingredients: 1 tbsp chopped dill, mint or coriander
steps: Hang curd in a muslin cloth for 3-4 hours to drain.
Whisk until smooth and creamy.
Add garlic, herbs, pepper, oregano and salt.
Stir in lemon juice.
Chill 15 minutes and serve with vegetable sticks.

title: Tomato Garlic Chutney
intro: A tangy, spicy South Indian chutney of roasted tomatoes, garlic and dry red chillies, finished with a mustard tempering. It has no sugar and only a few drops of oil. It pairs beautifully with dosa, idli and chilla. Keeps for four days in the fridge.
steps: Heat a few drops of oil and roast garlic and red chillies for a minute.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy.
Cool and blend with salt into a smooth chutney.
Heat remaining oil, crackle mustard seeds, curry leaves and hing.
Pour the tempering over the chutney.

title: Roasted Chana Peanut Chutney
intro: A creamy, protein-rich chutney made with roasted chana and a few peanuts instead of coconut. It has a lovely nutty taste and thick texture. Serve with idli, dosa or upma. A spoon of curd makes it extra smooth.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp mustard seeds and 6 curry leaves
steps: Blend chana, peanuts, chilli and ginger with a little water.
Add curd and salt and blend again until smooth.
Transfer to a bowl.
Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over and serve.

title: Beetroot Hummus
intro: A vibrant pink dip of chickpeas blended with roasted beetroot, garlic, toasted sesame and lemon. It is rich in protein, fibre and antioxidants. Use it as a spread in wraps or as a dip for vegetables and roasted papad. It looks stunning on the table.
steps: Blend sesame seeds to a coarse powder.
Add chickpeas, beetroot, garlic, lemon, cumin and salt.
Blend until smooth, adding ice water as needed.
Transfer to a bowl and swirl the top.
Drizzle olive oil and serve.
